# Fixtures

Small files the suites read. Real ones, not synthetic, because the bugs are
in real files.

| file | what it is for |
|---|---|
| `pGro7.gb` | a chaperone vector whose CmR gene is reverse-strand, spliced **and** crosses the origin — all three at once, which is the case the read-interpretation module's own documentation names as the hard one |
| `pRSFDuet-1.dna` | a SnapGene binary file, for the `.dna` reader. pRSFDuet-1 is a published Novagen/Merck product and its sequence is distributed by the manufacturer; this is a vector map of it, included as a format sample. |
| `Primer_stock.tsv` | an oligo inventory in the shape a lab's own spreadsheet comes in — **generated**, see below |
| `Plasmid_stock.tsv` | the same for a plasmid collection — **generated** |
| `Competent_cells.tsv` | the same for a strain list — **generated** |
| `make-stock-fixtures.js` | writes those three. Run it to regenerate them. |

## The three stock sheets are generated, on purpose

They were a real lab's inventory: 874 actual oligo sequences with their
freezer positions, and 854 real constructs with their targets, designs,
concentrations and boxes. That is unpublished research data and a map of what
a lab is working on, and it does not belong in a public repository however
convenient a fixture it made.

What the suites reading them actually test is the **importer**: that it finds
the sequence column in a sheet laid out the way a lab's own spreadsheet is,
that it recognises vector families, that it counts what it read, that it
refuses a primer binding twice in a Duet vector, that it reports a stretch
nothing can read. None of that depends on whose oligos they are.

So the shape is kept exactly and the content is invented. Kept: the header
lines — including `Sequence 5′→3′` with the arrow, which the reader once
failed to recognise, importing 874 oligos named after their freezer
positions; the three-part location in one cell; real published vector and
strain names, because recognising those is the point; the universal primers
every lab has, including T7 promoter, which a Duet vector binds twice. Thirty
oligos are taken from `pRSFDuet-1.dna` and clustered in its first two thirds,
so the sequencing planner has real matches to find and a real gap to report —
which is also how a lab's inventory is actually shaped.

Everything else — oligo sequences, gene names, freezer positions, construct
IDs — is generated by `make-stock-fixtures.js` from a fixed seed, so the
files are reproducible and obviously synthetic.

The larger corpus — real and deliberately malformed GenBank, EMBL, SnapGene
and ABI files — is **not** here. It is Biopython's `Tests/` directory, fetched
at validation time; see `tests/README.md`. Keeping it out makes its
provenance obvious and keeps this repository small.
